I inspected the repository architecture, OMP’s entry point/protocol/tests, the root and agent READMEs, and the current external-agent protocol. The working tree already has unrelated settings changes; I will leave them untouched.

Proposed small addition:

- Add a tiny reusable `llm` Go module with a provider-neutral `Generator` interface (`Generate(ctx, prompt, model)`), plus a function/mock adapter for unit tests.
- Include an optional command-backed implementation configured by environment variables, so no API key or SDK is embedded. It would send the prompt on stdin and pass the requested model through a `{model}` argument placeholder.
- Integrate it into the existing OMP agent only, via the protocol’s already-defined `text_generator` capability:
  - `info` advertises it only when an LLM command is configured.
  - new `generate-text --model …` forwards Entire’s summary prompt to the injected generator.
  - normal agents and tests require no credentials and make no network calls.
- Add a focused unit test proving model/prompt forwarding and JSON protocol output using the mock.
- Briefly document this optional summary-provider path in the root README.

This builds on the existing protocol instead of duplicating the framework, and makes OMP usable as an Entire `--summarize-provider` when configured.
